Proportional tax is a tax imposed at the same rate for everyone, regardless of their ability to pay. GST is imposed at the same rate for everyone, regardless of their ability to pay. For example, the GST rate is 10% for everyone. Therefore, GST can be categorised as a proportional tax.On the other hand, an indirect tax is a tax that is not paid directly by the person who bears the economic burden of the tax. In Australia, GST is an indirect tax as the businesses that charge GST are usually able to claim it back as an input tax credit. Therefore, the economic burden of the tax is borne by the end consumer who cannot claim the GST back. On the other hand, a consumption tax is a tax imposed on goods and services rather than on income. In Australia, GST is a consumption tax as it is imposed on the consumption of goods and services rather than on income. Therefore, the correct answer is E, as all of the above are correct.
